mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1400, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields in equities.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, signaling a tight labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in the previous month, the combined effect predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, due to increased consumer spending and business investment.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in two consecutive months signals strengthening supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as manufacturers and suppliers benefit.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2.0% signals weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as investors anticipate reduced consumer and business spending.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP growth and stock market correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increasing by more than 50 basis points in a single month, indicating monetary tightening, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher borrowing costs reduce investment and consumption.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances following the trigger, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in two consecutive months and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows to less than 50,000, the combined effect predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, due to decreased consumer spending power.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.5pp for 2 months and PAYEMS growth < 50,000
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market downturns and stock market performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) growth exceeding 5% in a single month, signaling strong consumer demand, always predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors react to the immediate boost in economic activity.
evidence_refs: fact:historical retail sales and stock market correlation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following RSAFS growth > 5%.
